mechanism_draft.text: Pipeline mechanism (six stages): (1) Offline Tri-Graph construction: extract entities from corpus passages via NER; create three node types (entity, sentence, passage); link via occurrence edges only — contain edges (passage→entity) and mention edges (sentence→entity); no relation triples are stored. (2) Query preprocessing: extract initial seed entities from the query; compute a query–sentence similarity vector to capture contextual relevance for each sentence in the graph. (3) Iterative entity activation: propagate activation scores through the sentence–entity subgraph; at each iteration, aggregate similarity signals from neighboring sentences to activate intermediate bridging entities that were not directly matched. (4) Dynamic threshold pruning: after each propagation round, discard entities whose activation falls below a running threshold, preventing combinatorial explosion of the active set. (5) Personalized PageRank on the passage–entity subgraph: seed the PPR with the activated entity set; initialize passage-node scores with a hybrid value combining direct query–passage similarity and entity-based evidence (i.e., the sum of activated-entity contributions mapped to their containing passages). (6) Retrieve top-k passages ranked by final PageRank score. The branching between vectorized and non-vectorized retrieval paths is governed by a configuration flag; the weighted aggregation of entity and passage contributions follows a sum-based formula with threshold masking applied to exclude sub-threshold terms. The intended mathematical role of the aggregation is a weighted sum over contributing entity and passage terms, where each term is gated by a threshold mask that zeros out weakly activated contributions before summation. The repository equation for this formula is a placeholder; the author should supply the concrete weighted-sum expression with explicit weight parameters and threshold symbol. The configuration flag determines whether the vectorized path (batched matrix operations) or the fallback path is taken at runtime; both paths converge on the same node_weights output. The spans in the source confirm the branching, formula computation, and weight-loading steps occur in a contiguous block of the graph_search_with_seed_entities method.

mechanism_draft.text: Offline graph construction stage: The index method first checks whether new passage hash IDs are present (branching on the length of the new-passage list). If new passages exist, it invokes extract_nodes_and_edges, passing in the existing passage-to-entity and sentence-to-entity mappings. The extraction routine returns entity nodes, sentence nodes, a passage-hash-to-entities mapping, and two adjacency structures: entity-to-sentence and sentence-to-entity. These adjacency structures are stored as sparse matrices representing the contain (passage–entity) and mention (sentence–entity) relationships. A threshold mask is applied during the branching logic: values that fail the comparison (i.e., passages already indexed) are excluded from further processing, ensuring idempotent incremental indexing. Its distinguishing design choice is the elimination of error-prone relation extraction: the graph index is built exclusively from entity-based occurrence edges (contain and mention), not from semantic relation triples.
